newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya-Moscow ties coming under threat -- Udugov.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya-Moscow ties coming under threat -- Udugov.

text.p: A senior Chechen official on Wednesday accused "influential groupings" in Moscow of trying to sabotage a planned meeting between President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov.

First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov said Russian fighter planes had simulated an attack on the central market and airport in the regional capital Grozny on Wednesday but Russian officials denied any such incident had taken place.
"The aim of these provocative actions by Russian military aircraft is to undermine the trip of Maskhadov (to Moscow)," Udugov told reporters.
"The incident demonstrates that there are sufficiently influential groupings in Moscow that want a continuation of the conflict (between Russia and Chechnya)," he added.

Udugov said he had filed a formal complaint with the Russian authorities, adding that officials in the Russian Security Council had told him the planes came from a military training school at Armavir.
Security Council officials were not immediately available for comment but Interfax news agency quoted a Russian airforce spokesman as saying no flights over Chechnya had taken place.

In a bizarre twist, sources in Chechnya's Interior Ministry told Reuters earlier the plane was actually Chechen and that it had been rehearsing for a parade to mark the republic's Independence Day on September 6.
The sources mentioned only one plane while Udugov was speaking about several.
In Moscow on Wednesday President Boris Yeltsin reaffirmed his wish to meet Maskhadov in the near future but no date or venue was announced.

Russian news agencies quoted Yeltsin as saying Moscow must fulfil all its obligations under agreements it has signed with the breakaway region, including the release of funds to help rebuild Chechnya's shattered economy and infrastructure.
"We have to fulfil what we promised," RIA Novosti news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying during a meeting in the Kremlin with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"Otherwise extremists (in Chechnya) criticise Maskhadov," the president added.
Kremlin sources said the meeting was likely to take place on Friday or Saturday.

Udugov said his own visit to Moscow to prepare the ground for Maskhadov's trip, originally scheduled for Thursday, was now in doubt. He said he would consult Maskhadov later on Wednesday to discuss whether it should go ahead.

Wednesday's row underlined the still widespread jitters in Chechnya about Russia's intentions a year after the two sides signed a peace pact ending their bloody 21-month conflict in which tens of thousands of people were killed.
Talks aimed at normalising relations between Moscow and Grozny are stalled over the vexed issue of Chechnya's status, left unresolved when Russia withdrew its troops.
Maskhadov, buoyed by the separatists' battlefield victory, insists that his republic is fully independent but Yeltsin wants Chechnya to remain loosely within the Russian Federation.
